title: Deploying AI Models on Edge GPUs: The Practical Challenges
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Getting a large language model running on an edge platform is relatively easy today. Open-source frameworks such as llama.cpp have made it possible to download a model, run inference and demonstrate results in a matter of minutes.

Optimising that deployment is where the real work begins.

A model may run correctly, yet still deliver disappointing throughput, consume more memory than expected or leave significant performance untapped. Understanding why requires looking beyond benchmark numbers and examining how the workload interacts with the underlying hardware and software stack.

Questions quickly emerge. Is GPU acceleration being used effectively? Does a different quantisation format offer a better balance of accuracy, memory footprint and performance? Which parts of the workload benefit most from GPU execution, and where are the bottlenecks?

These challenges are becoming increasingly relevant as AI workloads move onto edge devices, where memory, power and cost constraints are far stricter than in the datacentre.

In an upcoming webinar on 11 November, an Engineering Director from Imagination Technologies will walk through practical examples of porting, analysing and optimising AI models on edge GPU platforms. Using real workloads and open-source software, we'll examine the steps involved in moving from a working demo to a more efficient implementation, covering topics such as model quantisation, GPU offloading strategies and performance analysis.

The session is intended for software developers, AI engineers and system architects who want a better understanding of how modern AI workloads behave on edge hardware and what can be done to improve performance.

If you're working on edge AI and want to understand not just whether a model runs, but why it performs the way it does, this webinar should be worth your time.
